The petitioners are aggrieved by the second respondent's order dated 24.01.2020 seizing the R.O.

sentences.text: It is undisputed that the second respondent has initiated the aforesaid proceeding for seizure of R.O. water units without any notice to the petitioners.

The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the first petitioner is a charitable trust and has installed a Water Filter Plant to facilitate pure drinking water to the villagers of Halekote village at low cost as the villagers could be vulnerable to various water borne diseases and other health impediments.

The first petitioner, for installation of such water filter plant, has obtained permission from the concerned Gram Panchayath and additionally, the respondent No.3, after testing the water for potability, has issued a Certificate along with endorsement that the water is potable.
But, the second respondent, without even as much as a show-cause notice, has seized the water filter units on 24.01.2020.
The second respondent should have considered these circumstances.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that the first petitioner has installed the R.O. water plant for the use of the community on non- profitable basis and does not deal with packaged water.

A Certification from Bureau of Indian Standards would be required only when water is sold as packaged drinking water, and if a facility is set up for the benefit of the community for disbursing water in cans, ISI certification would not be required.

4. A Division Bench of this Court in Lochamesh B Hugar v. Union of India and others reported in (2013) 2 KLJ 643, relying upon the provisions of Food and Safety Standards (Food Products,
Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011, more specifically regulation 2.10.8, has directed the Authorities to ensure that all necessary steps are taken to prohibit, prevent, manufacture and sale of packaged drinking water without Certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards with further directions.

entities.text: Lochamesh B Hugar v. Union of India and others reported in (2013) 2 KLJ 643
entities.label: PRECEDENT

Food and Safety Standards (Food Products,
Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: However, after the decision of the Division Bench, it is undisputed that the Regulation 2.10.8 of the Regulations 2011 has been amended.

5. It is undisputed that the provisions of Regulation 2.10.8 of the Regulations 2011 prior to its amendment, as declared by the Division Bench in the aforesaid decision, contemplated Certification from Bureau of Indian Standards, but with the amendment, the definition of "packaged drinking water" has been altered.

The amendment reads as follows:
"2.10.8 Packaged Drinking Water (other than mineral water) - 1. means water, other than natural water that is likely to be used for human consumption and that is offered or sold in packaged form, by whatever name it may be called, offered or sold"
This Court, in the light of the amended provisions, in a similar matter in W.P.No.45574/2018 has held as under:-
"9.
Thus, from perusal of the amended Clause 2.10.8, it is evident that if the water is not sold for human consumption in packaged form, there is no requirement of obtaining the ISI Certificate.

However, the aforesaid aspect of the matter was not taken note by the learned Single Judge while deciding W.P.Nos.14176-80/2018 and 14638/2018 vide order dated 27.06.2018 and reliance was placed on the Division Aradhya Foundatino Charitable Trusts vs State Of Karnataka on 23 March, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165497867/
3

entities.text: Division Aradhya Foundatino Charitable Trusts vs State Of Karnataka on 23 March, 2020
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Bench decision of this Court in which Clause 2.10.8 as it existed at the time of decision of the writ petition was taken note of.
However, subsequently, the legal position has changed.
Therefore, neither the decision rendered by the Division Bench of this Court nor by the learned Single Judge of this Court apply to the fact situation of the case.

Since the petitioner is not selling the water in a packaged form, therefore,
he is not required to obtain ISI certificate.
In view of the preceding analysis, the impugned Annexures-B, D and H are hereby quashed."

6. In the light of the aforesaid amendment and the decision, the second respondent could not have seized the R.O. water plant set up by the petitioners on the ground that Certification from Bureau of Indian Standards is not obtained.
As such, the impugned order of seizure is liable to be quashed.

However, this Court is of the considered view that the authorities, within the limits of law, will have to ensure that proper hygienic conditions are maintained and necessary reports are obtained as regards quality of water for its potability.
In the light of the above, the writ petition is allowed.

The impugned annexures are set aside,
directing the second respondent to take appropriate action to enable the petitioners to restore its RO Water Plant while observing that every care and caution is taken to ensure hygiene and potability of water.
